Calculate the kinetic energy, potential energy, total energy and binding energy of an artificial satellite of mass 2000 kg orbiting at a height of 3600 km above the surface of the Earth.
Given:- \(G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\) Nm\(^{2}\)/kg\(^{2}\)
\(R = 6400\) km
\(M = 6 \times 10^{24}\) kg
_note: The printed answer set is INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT and PE is wrong. With r = R + h = 10^7 m and GMm = 8.004e17: KE = +40.02e9 J, PE = -80.04e9 J, TE = -40.02e9 J, BE = +40.02e9 J. The book prints PE = -80.09e9 (a digit slip for -80.04e9) which then propagates into its TE = -40.07e9; and its own TE and BE contradict each other, since BE = |TE| but it prints 40.07 and 40.02. Only PE and TE are wrong; KE and BE are right.
